questions.question_text: Which of these is best modelled by a normal random variable?

options.text: The masses of $5000$ eggs chosen at random from a farm.
The number of heads obtained in a single toss of three coins.
options.why: A count with only four possible values is discrete, so it has no continuous bell shape.

options.text: The times customers spend being served, where most are quick but a few take very long.
options.why: A long tail on the right makes the distribution skewed rather than symmetrical.

options.text: The last digit of $5000$ phone numbers chosen at random.
options.why: Every digit is equally likely, giving a flat distribution with no central peak.

questions.solution_text:
Mass is a continuous quantity that clusters about one central value, with unusually light and unusually heavy eggs about equally rare.
The masses of $5000$ eggs chosen at random from a farm are best modelled by a normal random variable.

questions.question_text: In a normal distribution, what is $P(X>\mu)$?

options.why: The mean divides the distribution into two equal halves, not zero probability on one side.
There is no asymmetry that would give two-thirds above the mean.
For every normal distribution, symmetry about the mean fixes this probability.

questions.solution_text: A normal distribution is symmetric about its mean. Exactly half of the area lies above $\mu$, so $P(X>\mu)=0.5$.

questions.question_text: In a normal distribution, what proportion of the data lies above the mean?

options.why: A normal distribution has values on both sides of its mean.
Confuses the proportion within roughly one standard deviation with the half above the mean.
Confuses the central two-standard-deviation proportion with one side of the mean.

questions.solution_text: The normal distribution is symmetric about its mean. Therefore half of the probability lies above the mean, so the proportion is $\frac12$.
